hook.line: Everyone in Bogotá asks the new arrival the same thing: have you got used to the altitude, the traffic, the food? You will want the right verb for it.
hook.es: Ya me acostumbré a la comida.
hook.en: I've got used to the food now.

examples.es: Mariana se adaptó al horario de la oficina.
examples.en: Mariana adapted to the office schedule.

examples.es: Ya me acostumbré a la comida.
examples.en: I've got used to the food now.

examples.es: Fue un periodo de adaptación difícil.
examples.en: It was a difficult period of adjustment.

examples.es: Tomás se adaptó rápido a la ciudad.
examples.en: Tomás adapted quickly to the city.
Have you got used to the traffic yet? (to a friend)

examples.es: Todavía no me acostumbro al ruido de la calle.
examples.en: I still haven't got used to the noise of the street.

rule:
Two verbs cover "adapting": *adaptarse a* and *acostumbrarse a*. Both are reflexive (*me, te, se, nos*) and both are followed by *a*:
*me acostumbré a la comida*
*se adaptó a la ciudad*

Before *el*, *a* joins it: *al horario*, *al ruido*. Before a verb, *a* stays: *me acostumbré a vivir lejos*.

English says "adapt to" and "used to", and some learners drop the *a*. Do not. The noun is *adaptación*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a verb with a fixed preposition: the *a* belongs to the verb.

readAndPick.es: Ya me acostumbré a la comida.
options: I've got used to the food now.
I still haven't got used to the food.
I'm used to cooking the food.

readAndPick.es: Todavía no me acostumbro al ruido de la calle.
options: I've got used to the street noise now.
I'll never hear the street noise.
I still haven't got used to the street noise.

readAndPick.es: Tomás se adaptó rápido a la ciudad.
options: Tomás wants to adapt to the city.
Tomás adapted quickly to the city.
Tomás is slowly adapting to the city.

readAndPick.es: Me acostumbré a vivir lejos de la familia.
options: I got used to living far from family.
I moved far from family.
I miss living with family.

readAndPick.es: Vale se adaptó a una cocina más grande.
options: Vale wants a bigger kitchen.
Vale adapted to a bigger kitchen.
Vale is adapting to a smaller kitchen.

readAndPick.es: Fue un periodo de adaptación difícil.
options: It was a difficult trip.
It was a difficult time for the café.
It was a difficult period of adjustment.
Children adapt quickly.
Children adapted quickly.
Children will adapt quickly.

readAndPick.es: Me acostumbré a tomar tinto sin azúcar.
options: I stopped drinking black coffee.
I got used to drinking black coffee without sugar.
I want to drink black coffee.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *a* or *de* and type the whole sentence: *Me acostumbré ___ la comida.*
Pick *al* or *el* and type the whole sentence: *Mariana se adaptó ___ horario.*
Say: I still haven't got used to the noise.
yourTurn.answer: Todavía no me acostumbro al ruido.
accept: No me acostumbro al ruido todavía.
yourTurn.why: *Me acostumbro* is the *yo* form, followed by *a* + *el* = *al*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Tomás adapted quickly to the city.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás se adaptó rápido a la ciudad.
accept: Tomás se adaptó a la ciudad rápido.
yourTurn.why: *Se adaptó* is reflexive, and *a la* comes before the thing he adapted to.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Have you got used to the traffic yet?
yourTurn.why: *Te* matches *tú* and the verb ends in *-aste*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about us: *Me acostumbré a la comida.*
Ask it as a question to a friend: *Me acostumbré al clima.*

pitfalls.why: English "used to" tempts other words, but this verb always takes *a*.
The *a* stays in front of an infinitive too.

personal: Say one thing you have got used to, or have not yet, with *me acostumbré a…* or *no me acostumbro a…*.
